quest.title: Those We Have Lost
quest.description: Before meeting her friends, she seems intent on resolving "anomalies" within herself first...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x625, Mora x53900, Hero's Wit x6, Mystic Enhancement Ore x12

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Ah, you're here. We should get going, then. Xavier and the others should be filming soon.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: How's it going? Have you managed to figure out the location of your home yet?

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: I've narrowed down a few potential locations.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: We just need to take a sample from each one. Once the equipment analyzes them, we should know the exact location and where to find the entrance.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Great! We should get started then!

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Alright. Let's get a move on.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: That should do it. Let's head back. The filming should be just about done.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: We made good time. We might even know the location by the end of the day!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You sound pretty happy about that!

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Do I? I suppose I've just had enough of these "anomalies" I've been dealing with. The sooner I can fix them the better.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Anyway, enough chitchat. We have work to do.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Oh, but let's head in through the side door. I don't want to run into the crew on the deck.

talks.objective: Return to the captain's cabin of the Wingalet

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Alright, now we just need to wait for the results.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Since we have some time to kill, I suppose I might as well see how this aquarium of yours is coming along. You seemed quite enthusiastic about it, after all.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hehe, it's really coming together!

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Oh. Kind of impressive, actually.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: These must be the ones we caught the first time we went underwater.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Like it?

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: ...Hmph. It's fine, I guess. Nothing special.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Come on! It sounded like you really liked it just now!

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: You're that proud of it? Is this the sense of accomplishment, or something?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, yeah... And it's pretty!

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: You know it's gonna be gone soon, though, right?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What do you mean?

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: After the Festival, this ship will be returned to the Fortress of Meropide, and this aquarium will be no more.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So?

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: So, no matter how much work you put into this place, once the festival is over, it's all just going to disappear.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But, not making the most of it when we have the chance is an even bigger waste!

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: But, if you know it's all going to be gone one day, why even bother?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, because... because...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Because you still get to keep the things you gain along the way, and those are things that can never be replaced.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Doesn't that make losing them even harder?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, if you put it like that...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But the happy memories we make along the way last forever! You just have to take a more... glass half-full perspective!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Not to mention, everything we do here is gonna be on film, so it'll still live on in some shape or form.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: And when you look back on it, only happy memories will come to mind?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Exactly!

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: So, it's about finding joy in the process itself... Hmm...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}!? You're back already!?

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: What's wrong with that? You say that like it's terrible news or something...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: How did you get here!? I didn't see you on the deck!

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Oh, never mind! We need to help Miss Guillotin hide ASAP! The crew is heading over here to shoot any second!

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: What? They should be done by now...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: *sigh* There was a mishap earlier that cost them some time. I was waiting on deck so I could warn you the minute you showed up!

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Anyway, you should head back to the captain's cabin right away! They're gonna be here any minute now!

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: ...Finally! That's a wrap for the scenes on the deck. Wouldn't have taken half as long if the wind hadn't snapped our equipment in two...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh oh, too late!

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Change of plans, then. You'll just have to hide!

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: H—Hide!? And where exactly am I supposed to do that?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...Oh! There's a box over there. You can get in that!

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Huh? You expect me to—

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: ...Do I need my makeup done for the next scene too?

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Tch... Ugh, for the love of—

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: Hm, let me see... Maybe just a quick touch-up.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: #Huh? {NICKNAME} and Paimon? What are you doing here? I thought you took the day off to take care of something?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Oh... W—Well, it didn't take as long as we were expecting, so we came back early! What about you guys? You're still not done shooting for the day?

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: No, we ran into an issue that set us back. It meant Miss Charlotte's crew wasn't able to wrap either. We both still have scenes to shoot in this aquarium.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh. Th—That's... not ideal.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: (For several reasons...)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let us help, then! The sooner we wrap, the sooner everyone can get some rest!

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Hehe. Alright.

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: Thanks, you two.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Miss Charlotte's crew can go first, then. If I'm not mistaken, you still have a night shoot later.

dialogues.speaker: Lepine-Pauline
dialogues.text: Thanks, Director Furina!

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Of course! Fellow artists should help each other out where we can!

dialogues.speaker: Lepine-Pauline
dialogues.text: Agreed! Well then, Kamera, lights, get set up! Actors, give your lines a quick once-over. Let's try to get this in one take!

dialogues.speaker: Lepine-Pauline
dialogues.text: Alright, places everyone. And three, two, one, action!

dialogues.speaker: "Hurlock"
dialogues.text: So, the story ends like this...

dialogues.speaker: "Gina"
dialogues.text: But when Duke St. Germanus departed, he clearly said that everything was beyond redemption...

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: (Huh? That sounds familiar... Wait, it's from that novel I came across while researching the numerological array...)

dialogues.speaker: "Hurlock"
dialogues.text: He's only a genius when it comes to mechanics; in everything else, he's just an ordinary person.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Tch...

dialogues.speaker: Lepine-Pauline
dialogues.text: (Huh? What was that noise? Whatever, I'll just fix it in post...)

dialogues.speaker: "Gina"
dialogues.text: ...Miss Jacoba! Please don't speak as if I were the accomplice!

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: (Not so hard! This box isn't sturdy enough for that!)

dialogues.speaker: "Hurlock"
dialogues.text: ...This is why I keep saying, 'Don't put too much trust in clockwork meka.' Unlike humans, machines don't have a heart.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: ...A heart?

dialogues.speaker: Alain Guillotin
dialogues.text: That's right. It's what's on the inside. It's also referred to as someone's soul, or likened to free will.

dialogues.speaker: Alain Guillotin
dialogues.text: You can think of it as a person's core — what makes them unique. In general, though, people don't believe machines are capable of having a soul.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: You said my emotion module was faultless.

dialogues.speaker: Alain Guillotin
dialogues.text: It is, but that's not quite the same thing.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Do you think I have one then? A heart?

dialogues.speaker: Alain Guillotin
dialogues.text: I don't think so.

dialogues.speaker: Alain Guillotin
dialogues.text: I know so.

dialogues.speaker: Alain Guillotin
dialogues.text: The question is, do you recognize it within yourself?

dialogues.speaker: "Gina"
dialogues.text: Hah, that's where you're wrong!

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: (Argh! I can't believe this! Forcing me to hide in a box and listen to this drivel... ME!)

dialogues.speaker: "Jacoba"
dialogues.text: In the end, clocks tick through tranquil years, fish swim in crystalline springs.

dialogues.speaker: "Jacoba"
dialogues.text: No matter how grand a dream is, it will fade away like this — forlorn, wordless, silent.

dialogues.speaker: Lepine-Pauline
dialogues.text: And cut!

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Whew! That was a long one... What did you think?

dialogues.speaker: Lepine-Pauline
dialogues.text: Hmm...

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: (If she makes them do another take, I'm going to flip a lid... and not just the one to this box!)

dialogues.speaker: Lepine-Pauline
dialogues.text: There were some weird audio things going on... But, acting-wise it was great! It's a keeper!

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: Perfect! That means...

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: (...I can get out of this box.)

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: It's our turn!

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Kamera operator, set up for the next scene.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: In this one, our protagonist peruses an aquarium in a foreign land and gets swept up in memories of her friend. So, in terms of lighting, that's the vibe we're going for. Got that?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: (Shoot, Paimon thought there'd be a break, and Sandrone could slip away... What are we gonna do now!?)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Guess she's just gonna have to hang in there a little longer...)

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: Break a leg!

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Yep, we're headed off to shoot our next scene!

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Alright, quiet on set! We're about to start rolling. Ready, Miss Columbina?

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Uh, ahem... Miss Columbina?

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: ...I think she would like this.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: (Quick! We should roll on this!)

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: It doesn't forage with the others or prey upon its smaller kin. Instead, it remains where it is — cradled in the coral's quiet beauty — as though the raging cyclones above are of no consequence.

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: And yet... she still stood before the cyclone in the end.

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: So I think that story has it wrong.

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: She is no different than us. She has a heart.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Columbina...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: (Uh oh, is she onto us!?)

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: (What is she doing?)

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Uh, ahem... Cut!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You okay, Columbina?

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: Hm? Oh, yes. I just thought...

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Why don't we take a short break? It's been a long day of shooting so far.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: That last take was beautifully organic, though. We can use it as is. No need to go again.

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: Thanks, Director Furina. But I'm fine to continue.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: You're sure? In that case, let's shoot some quick B-roll, then we can move to our next outdoor scene.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Phew, we're in the clear this time.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Tch, ugh! Absolutely suffocating...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You okay, Sandrone?

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: ...Right as rain.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: C'mon, let's go check the test results.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: It's time for me to go "home."

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Alright, it should be around here.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Give me some space. I'll activate the water-insulating mechanism.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The what...?

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Alain, much like Rene, had long predicted that the water levels in Fontaine would rise.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Thanks to his expertise in mechanics, he was able to implement a few simple measures to protect our home from flooding.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: I told him there was no need... that I would just move when the water rose too high.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: But, it would seem he knew a day like this would come.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, this is where you used to live? It's beautiful! There's even a garden!

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Back when I lived here, it was my job to tend to the potted plants and flower beds. Still growing strong even after all this time... Heh, who would've thought.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: If the weather was nice, I would take Alain out in his wheelchair, and we would go for a walk. Before long, we started bringing Pulonia along too.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Come to think of it, I was the only one who could get around easily back then. Pulonia always got stuck at some point, and it was up to me to launch a rescue mission.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Those sound like happy memories.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Happy? I suppose they were. Uneventful, but pleasant. Repetitive, but peaceful. It was like living in a world where time didn't exist.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Of course, that was all just an illusion. "Death" still awaits all of us at the end.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Alright, enough standing around. Let's head inside.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Yep, this place is exactly how I left it. Nothing has changed.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: Hm? What is it?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Your notebook...

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: Huh? How did you get— Oh, Arlecchino gave it to you, didn't she.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: And you... read the whole thing? Ahem... Just so you know, a lot of that was written a long time ago. At that very desk, to be exact.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: Hmph, anyway, since you've already read it, you should just hold onto it. I can always start a new one.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: Well, feel free to look around. I'm going to start looking for the "Gift" Alain mentioned.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: Oh, but be careful with the stuff around here. I'm not saying you can't touch anything. Just try not to choke on the dust.

choices.text: I have something to give back to you...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Some sort of mechanical workbench covered in all sorts of tools. Nothing a novice like me could make heads or tails of...)

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: This was Alain's workbench. Later on, of course, it became mine.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: It's where both Pulonia and I were brought to life.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Before Alain was bed-bound, this is where he would teach me about mechanics. I would sit and listen, chiming in with questions here and there.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Later on, when he got too sick, I took over and would work on Pulonia here.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (A few old toys that appear to be math-related... There are also some complex mathematical puzzles on the table...)

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Oh, I played with these when I was little.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: During the first few months after I was created, I mean.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: At first, Alain and I would play together, but it didn't take long for me to become unbeatable. So, Pulonia and I played together instead.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, uh... these don't look like Paimon's kind of games.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Heh, logic and math puzzles? Those happen to be my specialty.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: It's been so long... What do you say? Should we play a few rounds?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Sure. You pick the game.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Hm, let's go with this one. The gears on the left are stacked from largest to smallest. The goal is to move them to the other side in the fewest number of moves.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Just remember, you can't stack a bigger gear on top of a smaller one.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Need help? You seem stuck.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: This should go here... Then this here...

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: And done!

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Looks like it took you a few extra moves... My first attempt was the same. You'll get better with practice.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: You... managed to do it the fewest moves possible? Guess we can add puzzles to the list of things you're surprisingly good at.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Well? What did you think of the game?

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: You showed quite a bit of promise too. We should do this again sometime. There are other puzzles we could try.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: Well, these kinds of puzzles aren't for everyone. I suppose my upbringing wasn't exactly "conventional" in that sense...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (A faded old picture...)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, the people in this picture look kinda familiar.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Hm? Oh, this was taken when Alain and Rene were both still at the Fontaine Institute of Natural Philosophy. Before their falling-out.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: In his later years, Alain would often sit by the fireplace and stare at this picture, wearing an expression somewhere between "guilt" and "longing."

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: He said he sometimes regretted not helping his friend when he needed it most. Even if just to stop him.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Some yellowed pieces of paper... and what look like letters...)

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Oh, these are some of Alain's drafts from his later years. Just casual doodles, really.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: And these are just some unimportant letters. I couldn't be bothered to sort through them before I left.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, this house is filled with so many memories! It's so cozy and charming!

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Hmph, you should've seen it in its prime, when people actually lived here. A lit fireplace, a steaming cup of coffee... that's the real deal.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: You know, we also used to have a mechanical piano that Alain built.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oooh, how... chic!

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Alain never played it much. He probably wasn't able to at that point.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: But I managed to teach myself. Music theory is essentially math, after all. Once you learn the patterns, it's not really that difficult.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: I loved perusing Alain's collection of classical music. The chords and harmonies felt like individual mathematical puzzles. It was fascinating, so I did some composing as well.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: But as Alain continued to deteriorate, even the sound of music began to grate on his nerves. So I got rid of the piano.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh...

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Back then, I assumed a piano was like an ordinary clothing rack, commonplace in every home and easily replaceable. It was only after I left that I realized how hard a good piano is to find...

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Ahem, enough about that. Alain's gift should be just in here. The only things undisturbed before I left were a few of his personal belongings.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Wait, there's a hidden compartment at the back of this box... Looks like it's locked with some kind of gear mechanism...

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Knowing you, Alain, I'm guessing it goes like this... Then like this...

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Heh, got it. Am I a genius or what?

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Let's see here... A box?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well? You gonna open it?

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Hm, it's heavier than I was expecting. Just how much stuff is in here...?

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Hm? A letter? And a bunch of junk underneath it? None of it seems that important.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Ah, wait a second. This should be it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Um... a cube?

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: It's a "Multidimensional Algorithmic Core." Alain would use it to store information. Only Pulonia and I have access.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Alright, I'll start looking into the core and the letter. Feel free to go through the rest of this stuff and see if there's anything useful.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Okay! Hold on, there's another picture in here! This one has writing on the back...

dialogues.speaker: Alain Guillotin
dialogues.text: "... A snapshot of you playing among the plants shortly after you were born. You seem to like these flowers a lot. May you grow and flourish just as they do."

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Huh...?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow! Look how happy you are in this picture! You've changed a lot since then, huh...

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Wh—What's that supposed to mean!?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: J—Just that you come off kinda... aggressive, sometimes? Or, y'know, annoyed at... everyone around you?

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Well then, people should stop being so annoying! It's not like I'm the one with the problem!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Of course not...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, here's something else! Looks like a piece of paper torn out from somewhere.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: "...Today, I solved another math puzzle, and made a breakthrough on a construction problem the Institute has been stuck on for years. Am I a genius or what?"

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: No, wait! That's—

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: "From now on, I should have people address me as Her Highness the Clockwork Princess, Unraveller of All Reason!"

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: NO! Nope! No more of that. Ugh! I thought I tore this page out!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You wrote this? Then, how did it get... Wait, there's more writing at the bottom...

dialogues.speaker: Alain Guillotin
dialogues.text: "You seem to have developed a distaste for this particular entry, considering I found it in the trash. I'm sorry, but I could not help but hold onto it. Forgive me."

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Alain!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: D—Don't be embarrassed! Everyone goes through a phase like that.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Nonsense! I... I wasn't even the one who wrote that! It must have been Pulonia!

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: That's enough! I told you, it was Pulonia!

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: You know what? We're done with this. No more rifling around in the box!

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: Just put it down, and let me read the letter!

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: "To my little Clockwork Princess..." Oh, um...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Guess it's for Pulonia.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: Not another word. Got that!?

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: "If you're reading this..."

response.speaker: Alain Guillotin
response.text: "You've most likely received the 'gift' I left for you. I just hope you didn't stumble across all this while cleaning out my effects, or something trivial like that."

response.speaker: Alain Guillotin
response.text: "I once asked if there was something you wished for. Do you remember that? I wonder if time has changed your answer..."

response.speaker: Alain Guillotin
response.text: "Regardless, I have another gift — a formula that will allow you to come face to face with the 'anomaly' inside of you. Haha... if you even still call her that."

response.speaker: Alain Guillotin
response.text: "Why this gift? To understand that, allow me to wax poetic on the soul once again. I would ask you to stick with me until the end, but I know you will. You always have."

response.speaker: Alain Guillotin
response.text: "I believe a person should be born twice over in their lifetime. First, there's the birth that grants us life, then the birth of the soul."

response.speaker: Alain Guillotin
response.text: "It's a matter of transforming the life bestowed upon us into the life we choose for ourselves. And to do that, we must look inward.

response.speaker: Alain Guillotin
response.text: "We must make a conscious choice to define the meaning of our life, instead of allowing the happenstance of our existence to pass us by..."

response.speaker: Alain Guillotin
response.text: "This is the process of recognizing the 'soul' that lives within us."

response.speaker: Alain Guillotin
response.text: "You are my proudest masterpiece. I told you that long ago. But to me, you have never been a creation or a machine."

response.speaker: Alain Guillotin
response.text: "To me, you're just like the rest of us. You have a heart."

response.speaker: Alain Guillotin
response.text: "In fact, some theories think of the human brain as nothing more than a machine, and thought the product of its computations."

response.speaker: Alain Guillotin
response.text: "So, you see? Perhaps we're not so different, after all. Your inner machinery is just far more advanced than most."

response.speaker: Alain Guillotin
response.text: "No matter how one looks at it, the heart is a complex thing... a place where logic and reason collide with our emotions.

response.speaker: Alain Guillotin
response.text: "Your computational capacity allowed you to become sentient and develop logical reasoning. But it also granted you something that, on the surface, might seem contradictory — emotion."

response.speaker: Alain Guillotin
response.text: "Emotions and logic often clash with each other, and those instances of discord can accumulate over time. That is the source of what you refer to as the 'anomalies' within you."

response.speaker: Alain Guillotin
response.text: "As you told me once, you've always known what you don't want. Yet, you've never wished for anything in particular."

response.speaker: Alain Guillotin
response.text: "Similar to how a blind person can feel when a part of their bo{RUBY#[D]soul}dy is in pain, without being able to fully visualize its form. Such is your relationship with your soul."

response.speaker: Alain Guillotin
response.text: "So, what I leave you now is this... a formula that will allow you to see the shape of your soul. For if you want to protect your 'heart,' you must first be able to recognize it within yourself."

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: "Of course, whether you use it is entirely up to you. You are, and always have been, free to do as you wish."

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: "Regardless, whether by my formula or some other means, I trust you will know your heart one day. You always were a fast learner... and the smartest person I've ever known."

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: Alain...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: You alright?

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: ...I'm fine.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: I've already figured out how this formula works. Let's get out of here and then we can use it.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You made up your mind already? You're gonna do it?

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: Why wouldn't I? Resolving the "anomalies" within my core is the reason I came here in the first place.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Need our help?

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: No. I can do this on my own.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: But... do you want to watch?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh... What do you mean?

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: I already know what "anomaly" I need to resolve. Like Alain said, she's an amalgamation of all the times my logic algorithms have clashed with my emotions.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And by "resolve," you mean that literally, or...?

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: Yes.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But if you, uh, let us in like that, wouldn't that mean letting us see a bunch of your... y'know, inner thoughts and secrets...?

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: If what Alain said is true, then I'm about to be... born anew, or whatever. This is your chance to be lucky enough to witness it.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: Besides, you already read my whole diary. When it comes to keeping my innermost thoughts to myself... Well, I think that ship has sailed.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You're really sure about this?

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: Tch, how many times do I have to say it? I finally let you in as... friends, and you want to question it? I'm not gonna offer a second time.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: Enough with the mushy stuff. Just follow me.

choices.text: And thanks for saying that, Sandrone.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Alright, with the numerological array, I can construct a simple formula that will allow you to experience what I see and hear in real time.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh! Just like Citlali's sense-sharing technique! Been there done that!

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Huh, sounds like that Shaman has some tricks up her sleeve.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: The arcane and the mathematical are both fundamental laws of this world. Being able to achieve a similar result through both isn't surprising.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Anyway, let's get this show on the road.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: But no comments from the peanut gallery, okay? I know I offered, but I still don't want any interruptions.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Is this... my heart?

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: No, it's probably just the result of Alain's formula... a space dedicated to resolving "anomalies."

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Huh, but it looks like the walls are all... mirrors?

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: You made it. About time.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Is that me... from the past?

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: You just spoke of "anomalies"... Well, here I am. What happens when emotion contradicts reason.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Shall we sit down and talk?

dialogues.speaker: Alain Guillotin
dialogues.text: That should do it...

dialogues.speaker: Alain Guillotin
dialogues.text: Hello. My name is Alain Guillotin. Can you hear me?

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Brings back memories, doesn't it? The time we spent here.

dialogues.speaker: Alain Guillotin
dialogues.text: Here, I want you to have this.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: ...A notebook?

dialogues.speaker: Alain Guillotin
dialogues.text: You can use it to write things down.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: I don't need to write things down. I have unlimited memory.

dialogues.speaker: Alain Guillotin
dialogues.text: Even so, some things are more important than others, right? You can use it to write about the things that matter.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: So you wish me to carry out a basic priority sorting operation?

dialogues.speaker: Alain Guillotin
dialogues.text: Haha, I suppose you can think of it like that for now. But journaling is also an act of finding oneself.

dialogues.speaker: Alain Guillotin
dialogues.text: Much like we use wooden stakes to guide a plant to grow in a certain manner, what we choose to write down gives the soul much-needed direction.

dialogues.speaker: Alain Guillotin
dialogues.text: In the act of choosing what to forget and what to hold onto, we decide what kind of person we want to become.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Mmm... I don't understand. Like I said earlier, I don't need something like this.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: This is where we were born, where our life began.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Mornings of tending to the garden. Afternoons spent cleaning, reading, or studying. Evenings of cozying up by the fire, listening to Alain share stories about his past...

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Alain...

dialogues.speaker: Alain Guillotin
dialogues.text: Hm? What is it?

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: What are you drinking?

dialogues.speaker: Alain Guillotin
dialogues.text: Oh, this? It's coffee. It, uh... makes me more productive.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: I want to try it.

dialogues.speaker: Alain Guillotin
dialogues.text: Oh, okay... Here.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: ...Bitter.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Speaking of, why did you design me with senses? Taste, smell, touch...

dialogues.speaker: Alain Guillotin
dialogues.text: Well... I'm not quite sure. It just felt like the right thing to do.

dialogues.speaker: Alain Guillotin
dialogues.text: I suppose I hoped... you might have a life of your own one day, and that you deserve to experience all life has to offer.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Hm, still bitter. But the smell is nice.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Haha...

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: I thought those peaceful days would go on forever.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: You know that's not possible.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Maybe... But, how was I supposed to know the end was just around the corner...?

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: That was just bad luck.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Was it? Well, it certainly became a pattern, now didn't it...

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Over time, one of the habits we picked up from Alain was a love of coffee. We even took to hosting tea parties.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: A machine acting like a human... Kind of laughable, right?

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: I suppose... That's just what I'm used to.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Yeah. That's just what we're used to.

dialogues.speaker: Childe
dialogues.text: Hey, this place isn't half-bad! Great spot for a party.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Hmph... More and more people seem to be showing up to my tea parties uninvited. Anyone care to explain?

dialogues.speaker: Childe
dialogues.text: Can you blame me? I saw Columbina leading Capitano somewhere, and I had to see what that was about.

dialogues.speaker: "The Captain"
dialogues.text: I had simply asked Columbina where I might find Arlecchino. I have business to discuss with her, and Columbina suggested looking here.

dialogues.speaker: "The Captain"
dialogues.text: Tartaglia and I were unaware that this was a private gathering. Apologies for the intrusion. It won't be for long.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Tch, whatever. Just add it to the list of annoying things that have happened today. What's one more... Since you're here, you might as well stay for a cup of tea.

dialogues.speaker: Childe
dialogues.text: See? Told you she wouldn't mind.

dialogues.speaker: "The Captain"
dialogues.text: Much obliged, Sandrone.

dialogues.speaker: Signora
dialogues.text: Well, look who we have here. Good thing I brought extra desserts. This has turned into quite the occasion.

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: Capitano? I was just about to go find you.

dialogues.speaker: "The Captain"
dialogues.text: Pardon the intrusion. Rest assured, I won't sully your gathering with talk of work. We can have our discussion later.

dialogues.speaker: Signora
dialogues.text: Spoken like a true gentleman. A certain unmannered Eleventh seat could learn a thing or two.

dialogues.speaker: Childe
dialogues.text: Y'know, you really should start being nicer to me, Rosalyne, or I might just snatch that Eighth seat right out from under you.

dialogues.speaker: Signora
dialogues.text: Hah, I'd like to see you try.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: If you're gonna fight, take it outside. The only mess I plan on cleaning up is tea-related.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: (*nom nom nom*)

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: I still don't understand how our quiet afternoon turned into such a crowded gathering. One by one, people just kept barging in...

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: ...And then, one by one, they left without a word.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Yeah. Pretty annoying, huh...

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: Of all my days with the Fatui... The times I spent with you, Arlecchino, and Rosalyne... They were my favorite.

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: ...Goodbye, Sandrone.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: ...Don't go, Columbina.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Heh... we should have just said that. Why didn't we? If we had, would the story have had a different ending?

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: She couldn't stay. There was no future for her here. She would have just faded away.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: You're right. I suppose that's why you call me an "anomaly."

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Every time you make a decision, there's a voice inside your heart — my voice — asking to contradict all logic and reason.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Why didn't we make her stay? Is it worse to fight for something just to lose it, or not to have fought at all?

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Don't you find it unfair? One by one, we keep losing the things we care about the most.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: But, in the end, whether I want to fight for something or cry over all we've lost, you just push it down and pretend not to hear.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: And now, even Pulonia... the other half of Alain's legacy, the last remaining member of our family...

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Even Pulonia is no longer with us.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: I did everything I could, but it's just like Alain always said... Pulonia was one of a kind. There was no replicating what he managed to create.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Don't you feel like our connection to the past is fading bit by bit? Like even the things we have left are slowly slipping away?

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: I suppose.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: But you can't move through life without having to say goodbye. And even as we experience loss, there are always new things to be gained.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Heh... ever so logical.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Hmph. What's your take, then?

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: It feels like... the more I care about something, the faster the world takes it away.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Hah... It sounds so stupid. But, I can't help it. That's the hand life has dealt me time and time again.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Why even fight for something that's just going to be lost in the end... Better to never have had it at all... Better if it would all just disappear...

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Dark, I know. But the heart wants what it wants, heh... Maybe the Stellar Linchpin appeared because of me. Because of what I wish for...

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: I don't think so.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Heh... Yeah, probably not. What an "anomaly" wants goes against all logic and reason, after all...

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Well, go ahead and do what you came for. You're here to resolve the "anomaly," aren't you?

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Yes.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Hmm, what's it gonna be? Keeping me imprisoned here like before?

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Or eliminating me entirely, like debugging a code? Hah... That might actually be a mercy.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: I don't care. I just don't want to experience the pain of loss ever again...

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Go ahead. I'm ready.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...Sandrone.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: I'm fine.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Um... It's okay to cry, y'know.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Cry? You've gotta be kidding me. Save the comforting for someone who needs it, Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Just now, that was...

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: The emotional side of my core algorithm.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: My emotion module has always been fully developed and operational. Alain tried to tell me that too. I've just chosen to ignore her voice all this time.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Because of a fear of loss?

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: I suppose. Huh, come to think of it, it's kind of like the aquarium on the ship.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The aquarium?

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: The old me took one look at it and saw something I would inevitably lose, so I stopped putting in the effort.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Then, one by one, the fish all swam away, and the place became even more bleak and depressing. Heh, pretty pathetic, right?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Don't say that! A lot of people would feel the same. It just shows how much you care about what you have.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What about now?

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Now? Hm... After seeing what you've done with the aquarium, I have to admit... I think it's beautiful.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: It's like you said, we get to keep the things we gain along the way, and those are things that can never be replaced, because we choose to hold them in our hearts.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well said!

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Besides... I've already "died" once. I'd be stupid not to make the most of this second chance.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About your wish...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Right! Earlier you... or your inner self, mentioned something about her wish. What was it?

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Heh, you think that's something you can just ask, and I'll tell you? Think again.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: I may have accepted my emotional{RUBY#[D]anomalies} self, but I'm not about to go all soft and mushy on the inside and pour my heart out.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (...Yep, still the same old Sandrone.)

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: That said... taking a step in the right direction couldn't hurt... starting with cleaning some old aquarium tanks of my own.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh?

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Metaphorically speaking, I mean. C'mon, let's head back to the ship. I need to talk to that Shaman.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: ...Huh? Resentful lost souls?

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: You couldn't get comfortable sleeping near the Opera Epiclese, right? Well, I bet that's why. The Fountain of Lucine is where all the water in Fontaine gathers, so that's where the emotions within the water converge as well.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Hold on... If it's souls we're dealing with, feeling uncomfortable should have been just the beginning. I should have been able to hear their voices or something.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: And under normal circumstances, I'm sure someone of your talents would have. The problem is, these souls are no longer complete.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Remind me how they ended up like that again? You mentioned something about them being split apart?

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Yes. It's called soul-severing. Rene of the Narzissenkreuz Ordo came up with it.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: After learning of Fontaine's impending doom, Rene thought if he could find a means for the soul to live on in perpetuity, it might ensure the world's salvation. Soul-severing was the first step of his research.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Unfortunately, his theory of the Four Orthants was imperfect at the time, and a failure along the way caused his physical form to dissipate.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Jakob, another member of the Narzissenkreuz Ordo, sought to carry on Rene's legacy and restore his physical form. He even used some of the people who stood in his way as test subjects for his research.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: By severing their souls?

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Yes. After Rene successfully awakened, the two continued their research, and all the severed souls ended up merging into Rene's consciousness.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: After you saved Fontaine by turning Fontainians into true "humans," these souls returned to the Ley Lines.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: But the souls severed before Rene awakened had nowhere to go, doomed to forever wander the waters of Fontaine as listless spirits.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Almost as if they exist outside the bounds of this world... unrecognized by the Ley Lines or fate. No wonder I couldn't sense them.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Breaking free from fate... was also one of Rene's goals back then.)

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Not only that, but over time, they began to fuse with other entities. Their inner resentment lured in all sorts of evil beings, which corrupted and defiled them into nothing more than accumulations of filth.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: But the full transformation must have been recent. Otherwise, the Iudex surely would have noticed.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Wait, no, he must know already! That would explain the underwater Melusine patrols. No wonder I kept running into officers from the Marechaussee Phantom earlier!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: In that case, let's go find Neuvillette, and we can sort it out together!

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: No, not just yet.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Why not?

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: For one, the diplomatic hassle alone would be a nightmare. Even though I haven't reported back to Snezhnaya yet, I'm not planning to leave the Fatui anytime soon.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Heh, besides, with me here, success is a done deal. Involving other people would just complicate things.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: All I need is for Miss Citlali to help pinpoint the location of this monstrosity. Think you can do it?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Pfft, with my eyes closed. This is what I do. I'm a lot better at it than manning a desk, at least.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: But, uh, how exactly do you plan on resolving this soul stuff? Even to me, there's no obvious answer. Seems pretty complicated, all things considered.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Just trust me. I have the perfect solution.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh, alright. If you're that confident, we'll follow your lead.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh, why the sudden interest in helping Fontaine with this, Sandrone? You never knew Rene and the others, right?

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: No, I didn't. And you're right, this problem has nothing to do with me. I wouldn't get within ten feet of the Narzissenkreuz Ordo or its members.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: But... In his later years, Alain told me he regretted not helping his best friend when he needed it the most.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: He also felt sorry towards Mary-Ann, for being too lost in his mechanical research to look after her properly.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: If he were still with us, I think he'd do the same. He might have a few choice words to say about it, but even after everything, he wouldn't leave his friend's mess for someone else to clean up.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Friends shouldn't hold grudges or leave behind regrets. Fixing what happened between him and Rene was one of his greatest wishes. All I'm doing is fulfilling it in his stead.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hehe, y'know, you really do seem a little different now.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Tch, you mean everything that just happened wasn't for nothing? Why, thank you for pointing out the obvious, Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Giving those aquarium tanks a good cleaning, huh...

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Hmph, just washing off the grime of the past. Turns out, a lot can build up after being ignored for so long.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: (What's this about aquarium tanks all of a sudden? They go off on some grand adventure, and what? Now they have their own private code? Hmph, stupid.)

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Alright then, Citlali. Tracking this thing down is up to you.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Huh? Oh... Right. No problem.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You've got this, Granny Itztli!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You've got this, Granny Itztli!

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Tch...! You! Come with me to Hotel Debord for a drink. Right now!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Wh—Why?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Why? Because I said so!

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Miss Guillotin, I'll report back on the location tomorrow morning. Just need a drink or two first to bolster me up.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Well... Don't let me keep you.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Alright, you. Time to go! I've got scores that need settling...

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: ...Huh?

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Listless, abandoned souls... an accumulation of resentment and filth...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Pulonia...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Old notes...

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: Coffee... tea...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: A warm hearth...
